A.q: Which verb form does an affirmative imperative use?
A.explain: Imperatives tell people to do things and can give instructions, directions, or advice. Affirmative imperatives use the base form. Past simple, present continuous, and third-person singular are not used.

A.q: To make an imperative negative, place which words before the verb?
A.explain: Negative imperatives put Don’t or Do not before the base form of the verb. Didn’t, Won’t, and Can’t are not used for negative imperatives.

A.q: Which statement is true about the form of an imperative verb?
options: The form is the same for one or many
The form changes for a group of people
You always add a subject to the verb
You always add to before the verb
A.explain: There is no difference if you give a command to a single person or to a group of people. The form of the verb is the same. Put the verb in the infinitive form without “to,” and you don’t use a subject.

A.q: Which is used to make an imperative sound more polite in formal settings?
options: Please or Could/Can you + the base verb
Would you mind + the base form of the verb
Could you + the -ing form of the verb
Please + the past simple form of the verb
A.explain: To sound more polite, especially in formal settings, use please and/or Could you or Can you followed by the base verb. 'Would you mind' takes the -ing form, 'Could you' takes the base form (not -ing), and please does not take a past simple form.

A.q: Which form matches Never send an email without a greeting?
options: Don’t send an email without a greeting
Didn’t send an email without a greeting
Won’t send an email without a greeting
Can’t send an email without a greeting
A.explain: Never gives emphasis and equals Don’t here. Always also gives emphasis in imperatives.

A.q: Which pattern expresses a suggestion or order with a time clause?
options: Time word + you + simple present, imperative
Time word + you + simple present, simple present
Time word + you + past simple, past simple
A.explain: Imperatives can follow time or if clauses. Use a comma when the main clause is second.

A.q: Which informal sentence assigns a task?
options: You write the e-mail and I will check it
You writes the e-mail and I will check it
You writing the e-mail and I will check it
You wrote the e-mail and I will check it
A.explain: You can use You with imperatives informally to decide who does what or add emphasis.

A.q: Which indefinite-pronoun imperative is correct?
A.explain: Somebody and Someone refer to one person; Everybody and Everyone refer to a group. They take the base verb.

A.q: Let’s is a kind of imperative that makes suggestions or gives instructions to other people in a group. Let’s equals which words?
A.explain: Let’s = let us. It is used for suggestions or instructions to other people in a group. Let me, let you, and let them do not match the contraction.

A.q: The affirmative form of Let’s uses which structure?
A.explain: Affirmative Let’s takes the base verb: Let’s stop there.

A.q: The negative form of Let’s uses which structure?
A.explain: Negative Let’s uses Let’s not + base verb: Let’s not talk about that now.

A.q: You can use Let’s to make suggestions to do things with other people or to give instructions, for example in class. You can soften Let’s with “just” in speaking. Which statement aligns?
A.explain: You can use Let’s to make suggestions (Let’s meet after class today) or give instructions (Let’s get started). Soften with just (Let’s just do this exercise). The other forms do not use the base form.

A.q: Which is a correct negative imperative?
A.explain: Negative imperatives use Don’t + base verb: Don’t shout at me. Past, continuous, and third-person forms are not used.

A.q: Which is a correct polite imperative?
options: Please tell me your phone number
Please tells me your phone number
Please told me your phone number
Please telling me your phone number
A.explain: Polite imperatives use Please + base verb: Please tell me your phone number. Other verb forms are incorrect.

A.q: Which time-clause sentence gives an order?
options: When you feel bored, go to the cinema
When you feel bored, you go to the cinema
When you felt bored, go to the cinema
When you feeling bored, go to the cinema
A.explain: Orders and suggestions use an imperative main clause: When you feel bored, go to the cinema. Facts use simple present in both clauses.

A.q: Which is correct for a group?
A.explain: Group imperatives with Everybody or Everyone use the base verb: Everybody open your book. Singular, past, and continuous forms are not used.

A.q: Which Let’s sentence is a suggestion?
A.explain: Let’s + base verb makes a suggestion: Let’s meet after class today.

A.q: Which fill-in is correct for a negative imperative meaning do not be afraid?
A.explain: Don’t + base verb be.

A.q: Which is a correct Let’s suggestion for a cold room?
A.explain: 'Let’s' takes the base verb close.

A.q: Which sentence correctly uses always to give emphatic advice?
A.explain: Always + base verb makes an emphatic affirmative imperative. Wears, wearing, and wore are not imperative forms.

A.q: Complete the negative imperative: While you are at school, ___ off your mask.
A.explain: Never + base verb is used for emphatic negative imperatives. The correct form is never take.

A.q: Which polite request uses 'Could you'?
A.explain: Polite requests use Could you + base verb. Opens, opening, and opened are incorrect after could you.

A.q: Which is the formal negative imperative?
options: Do not stay out too late.
Do not stays out too late.
Do not staying out too late.
Do not stayed out too late.
A.explain: Formal negative imperatives use Do not + base verb. The base form stay is required.

A.q: Which sentence uses 'Please' correctly?
options: Hand out the books please to.
Please hand out to the books.
A.explain: 'Please' normally comes at the end of an imperative (usually after a comma). The other options have wrong word order or an unnecessary 'to'.

A.q: Which sentence keeps the same meeting rule?
options: Don't check your messages when you are in a meeting.
Don't checking your messages when you are in a meeting.
Not check your messages when you are in a meeting.
Don't check your messages when you are in a meeting, please to.
A.explain: The imperative can come before the time clause. The meaning is the same: Don't check your messages when you are in a meeting.

A.q: Which sentence gives an order or suggestion, not a fact or habit?
options: When you feel bored, go to the cinema.
When I feel bored, I go to the cinema.
When she feels bored, she goes to the cinema.
When we felt bored, we went to the cinema.
A.explain: Suggestions and orders use an imperative in the main clause: go. The other sentences state facts, habits, or past events.

A.q: Which is the correct emphatic negative imperative?
options: Don't you scare me like that again!
Doesn't you scare me like that again!
Didn't you scare me like that again!
Don't you scared me like that again!
A.explain: In informal emphatic imperatives, you can appear after Don't: Don't you scare me... The verb remains in base form.

A.q: Choose the sentence with the same meaning: If you are expecting a call, tell the other people in the meeting.
options: Tell the other people in the meeting if you are expecting a call.
Tell the other people in the meeting if you are expecting a call, .
Telling the other people in the meeting if you are expecting a call.
Tell the other people in the meeting if you are expecting a call to.
A.explain: The imperative can come before the if-clause. No comma is needed before if in this structure.

A.q: It's raining. Choose the correct suggestion.
A.explain: Let's + base verb makes a suggestion. The correct form is Let's take.

A.q: I'm thirsty. ___ some water.
A.explain: The suggestion form is Let's + base verb: Let's drink some water.

A.q: Which correction fixes the negative form?
options: Don't send text messages during class.
Do not sending text messages during class.
Doesn't send text messages during class.
Not send text messages during class.
A.explain: The correct negative imperative uses Don’t + base verb. Do not sending is wrong because not must be followed by the base verb, Doesn’t is not used for commands, and Not send is incomplete.

A.q: ___ your mobiles before the exam.
A.explain: Imperatives use the base verb: Switch off your mobiles.

A.q: The music is too loud. ___ it down.
A.explain: The imperative uses the base verb: Turn it down.

A.q: ___ your room before you leave.
A.explain: The imperative uses the base verb: Tidy your room.

A.q: ___ the door, please.
A.explain: The imperative uses the base verb: Shut the door.

A.q: Which imperative fits: ______ the wound clean and dry?
A.explain: Keep the wound clean and dry to prevent infection. Wash is for hands. Apply is for ointment. Elevate is for the leg.

A.q: Which imperative fits: _____ two tablets every six hours?
A.explain: Take two tablets of Panadol every six hours for fever. Drink is for fluids. Rest is in bed. Call is for emergency services.

A.q: Which imperative fits: _____ your hands before handling dressings?
A.explain: Wash your hands with soap and warm water before handling sterile dressings. Keep is for the wound. Apply is for ointment. Elevate is for the leg.

A.q: Which imperative fits: _____ the patient's blood pressure every two hours?
A.explain: Monitor the patient's blood pressure and pulse rate every two hours. Administer is for the dose. Sterilize is for equipment. Verify is for identity.

A.q: Which imperative fits: _____ all surgical equipment before entering the operation room?
A.explain: Sterilize all surgical equipment before entering the operation room. Monitor is for vital signs. Administer is for medication. Discontinue is to stop medication.

A.q: Which imperative fits: ______ the full dose of IV antibiotics?
A.explain: Administer the full dose of IV antibiotics. Monitor is for vital signs. Sterilize is for equipment. Verify is for identity.
